# 1) Setup

## - Defining work directory

In this section, we define the working directory for the R Markdown document.

```{r setup, include=TRUE}
# Get the path of the current script
# Then get the parent directory of the parent directory of the parent directory
local_wd_folder <- dirname(dirname(dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)))

# Set the root directory for knitr to the local working directory
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = local_wd_folder)
```

## - Defining input data and output directories

Here, we define the directories for input data and output files.

```{r}
data_folder <- paste(local_wd_folder, "/cohort_metadata", sep = '')
results_folder <- paste(local_wd_folder, "/results", sep = '')
```

Setting a seed ensures that any random processes are reproducible.

```{r}
# Set a seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)
```


## - Loading palettes

In this section, we load additional color palettes and define some custom ones.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load additional colour palette packages
library(unikn, quietly = TRUE)
library(RColorBrewer, quietly = TRUE)
library(yarrr, quietly = TRUE)
library(scales, quietly = TRUE)
library(ggsci, quietly = TRUE)

# Define a set of custom color palettes from the unikn package
mix_1 <- usecol(pal = c(Karpfenblau, "white", Peach), n = 15)
mix_2 <- usecol(pal = c(rev(pal_seeblau), "white", pal_pinky))
mix_3 <- usecol(pal = c(rev(pal_bordeaux), "white", pal_petrol), n = 15)

# Display the custom palettes
seecol(list(mix_1, mix_2, mix_3), col_brd = "white", lwd_brd = 4, title = "Comparing palettes mixed from unikn colors", pal_names = c("mix_1", "mix_2", "mix_3"))

# Define a second set of custom palettes from the RColorBrewer and yarrr packages
brew_mix <- usecol(c(rev(brewer.pal(n = 4, name = "Reds")), "white", brewer.pal(n = 4, name = "Blues")), n = 13)
brew_ext <- usecol(brewer.pal(n = 11, name = "Spectral"), n = 12)
yarrr_mix <- usecol(c(piratepal("nemo"), piratepal("bugs")))
yarrr_mod <- usecol(c(piratepal("ipod")), n = 9)

# Display the second set of custom palettes
seecol(pal = list(brew_mix, brew_ext, yarrr_mix, yarrr_mod), col_brd = "white", lwd_brd = 2, title = "Using usecol() and seecol() to mix and modify palettes", pal_names = c("brew_mix", "brew_ext", "yarrr_mix", "yarrr_mod"))

# Define additional custom palettes from the scales package
natjournals_palette <- pal_npg("nrc")(10)
```

# 2) Figure

Oncoprint

## - Loading input files

Here we load two CSV files containing clinical and mutation metadata.

```{r}
Clinical_metadata <- read.csv(paste(data_folder, '/Cohort_clinical_metadata.csv', sep = ''), row.names = 'Patient.ID')
Mutation_metadata <- read.csv(paste(data_folder, '/Cohort_mutation_metadata.csv', sep = ''), row.names = 'Patient.ID')
Laboratory_data <- read.csv(paste(data_folder, '/Cohort_laboratory_data.csv', sep = ''), row.names = 'Patient.ID')
Singlecell_data <- read.csv(paste(data_folder, '/Cohort_single_cell_metadata.csv', sep = ''), row.names = 'Patient.ID')

Clinical_metadata <- Clinical_metadata[rownames(Laboratory_data %>% arrange(-Blast.count)),]
Mutation_metadata <- Mutation_metadata[rownames(Laboratory_data %>% arrange(-Blast.count)),]
Singlecell_data <- Singlecell_data[rownames(Mutation_metadata),]
```

```{r}
Mutation_metadata <- Mutation_metadata
```

## - Heatmap

### - Cell geometry

All glyph dimensions are specified here in centimetres and the drawing fractions
are derived from them, so the figure is retuned by changing these five numbers
rather than by balancing interacting scale factors.

- `sq_side_cm` — side of the mutation square. The square stays square because
  its width and height fractions are computed separately against the cell box.
- `bar_h_cm` — height of the status bar under the square.
- `sq_bar_gap_cm` — vertical space between square and bar.
- `row_gap_cm` — blank space between adjacent gene rows.
- `col_gap_cm` — blank space between adjacent patient columns; increasing this
  widens the cell without changing the square.

```{r}
sq_side_cm    <- 0.40   # mutation square side
bar_h_cm      <- 0.09   # status bar height
sq_bar_gap_cm <- 0.07   # gap between square and bar (slightly increased from 0.04)
row_gap_cm    <- 0.12   # blank space between gene rows
col_gap_cm    <- 0.10   # blank space between patient columns

# Cell box dimensions implied by the above.
cell_w_cm <- sq_side_cm + col_gap_cm
cell_h_cm <- sq_side_cm + sq_bar_gap_cm + bar_h_cm + row_gap_cm

# Fractions of the cell box, used by the glyph functions. Width and height are
# derived independently so the square renders square in a non-square cell.
SQ_W_FRAC <- sq_side_cm / cell_w_cm
SQ_H_FRAC <- sq_side_cm / cell_h_cm
BAR_FRAC  <- bar_h_cm   / cell_h_cm

# The square + gap + bar block is centred vertically, so row_gap_cm splits
# evenly above and below it.
SQ_DY  <-  ((sq_bar_gap_cm + bar_h_cm) / 2) / cell_h_cm
BAR_DY <-  ((sq_side_cm + sq_bar_gap_cm) / 2) / cell_h_cm

# Annotation blocks share the column width, so their height is pinned to the
# same value to keep them square.
square_size <- unit(cell_w_cm, "cm")
```

### - Mutation matrix colors

Each mutation cell is drawn as a square sitting above a thin status bar.

The square is split along its bottom-left / top-right diagonal into two
triangles. The **top-left triangle** is filled dark grey when the gene carries a
variant reported in bulk; the **bottom-right triangle** is filled green when such
a variant was recovered by scDNA-seq. A variant seen on both platforms therefore
fills the whole square, while a bulk variant not recovered in single cells leaves
only the top-left half filled.

The **status bar** beneath the square is filled the same green as the
recovered-in-scDNA-seq triangle when the gene carries one or more variants
identified exclusively by scDNA-seq, and is neutral grey otherwise. The bar is
the only mark a novel variant makes: it does not fill the bottom-right triangle,
which is reserved for recovery of a bulk-reported variant. This is what
distinguishes a *TP53* cell where a single bulk variant was confirmed from one
where a bulk variant was confirmed **and** further variants were seen only in
single cells.

Cell values are semicolon-separated states from `Cohort_mutation_metadata.csv`:
`Bulk only`, `Recovered`, `Novel`. `Recovered;Novel` is the composite case above.

```{r}
# Blank / NA cells mean "no mutation detected in this gene".
Mutation_metadata[is.na(Mutation_metadata)] <- ''

# Split composite cells on ';' and trim whitespace.
get_type_fun <- function(x) trimws(strsplit(x, ";")[[1]])

# Glyph colours.
col_bulk  <- "grey25"     # top-left triangle: reported in bulk
col_sc    <- "#009E73"    # bottom-right triangle: recovered in scDNA-seq
col_novel <- col_sc       # status bar: novel scDNA-seq variant(s) present
                           # (matches col_sc — same green as the recovered
                           # triangle, rather than the previous dark blue)
col_bg_sq <- "grey93"     # empty square
col_bg_bar<- "grey85"     # empty status bar

# ---- Glyph drawing helpers --------------------------------------------------
# Each takes the (x, y, w, h) of a cell — or of a legend key — and derives its
# layout from the fractions above, so the legend keys are drawn by exactly the
# same code as the matrix cells and cannot drift out of sync.

# Top-left triangle: bottom-left -> top-left -> top-right.
draw_tri_bulk <- function(x, y, w, h, fill = col_bulk) {
  cy <- y + h * SQ_DY
  hw <- w * SQ_W_FRAC / 2
  hh <- h * SQ_H_FRAC / 2
  grid.polygon(
    x = unit.c(x - hw, x - hw, x + hw),
    y = unit.c(cy - hh, cy + hh, cy + hh),
    gp = gpar(fill = fill, col = NA)
  )
}

# Bottom-right triangle: bottom-left -> bottom-right -> top-right.
draw_tri_sc <- function(x, y, w, h, fill = col_sc) {
  cy <- y + h * SQ_DY
  hw <- w * SQ_W_FRAC / 2
  hh <- h * SQ_H_FRAC / 2
  grid.polygon(
    x = unit.c(x - hw, x + hw, x + hw),
    y = unit.c(cy - hh, cy - hh, cy + hh),
    gp = gpar(fill = fill, col = NA)
  )
}

# Status bar under the square.
draw_bar <- function(x, y, w, h, fill = col_novel) {
  grid.rect(
    x, y - h * BAR_DY,
    w * SQ_W_FRAC, h * BAR_FRAC,
    gp = gpar(fill = fill, col = NA)
  )
}

# Empty cell: pale square plus pale bar.
draw_background <- function(x, y, w, h) {
  grid.rect(
    x, y + h * SQ_DY,
    w * SQ_W_FRAC, h * SQ_H_FRAC,
    gp = gpar(fill = col_bg_sq, col = NA)
  )
  draw_bar(x, y, w, h, fill = col_bg_bar)
}

# ---- alter_fun --------------------------------------------------------------
# The two triangles describe the fate of bulk-reported variants only:
#   'Bulk only' -> top-left half, not recovered in scDNA-seq
#   'Recovered' -> both halves, reported in bulk and recovered in scDNA-seq
# 'Novel' marks only the status bar, so a gene whose sole findings are novel
# scDNA-seq variants shows an empty square above a green bar.
alter_fun = list(
  background = function(x, y, w, h) {
    draw_background(x, y, w, h)
  },
  `Bulk only` = function(x, y, w, h) {
    draw_tri_bulk(x, y, w, h)
  },
  `Recovered` = function(x, y, w, h) {
    draw_tri_bulk(x, y, w, h)
    draw_tri_sc(x, y, w, h)
  },
  `Novel` = function(x, y, w, h) {
    draw_bar(x, y, w, h)
  }
)

# oncoPrint still requires a named colour vector matching the alter_fun states,
# but the built-in legend cannot render composite glyphs, so it is suppressed
# and a hand-built legend (below) is passed to draw() instead.
col = c(
  "Bulk only" = col_bulk,
  "Recovered" = col_sc,
  "Novel"     = col_novel
)

# Define an empty column title
column_title = ""

# ---- Custom detection legend ------------------------------------------------
# Key boxes are scaled-up copies of the cell box, so they keep the cell's aspect
# ratio and the glyph fractions render identically.
legend_key_scale <- 1.4

lgd_detection <- Legend(
  title = "Variant detection",
  labels = c(
    "Reported in bulk",
    "Recovered in scDNA-seq",
    "Novel scDNA-seq variant(s)"
  ),
  graphics = list(
    function(x, y, w, h) {
      draw_background(x, y, w, h)
      draw_tri_bulk(x, y, w, h)
    },
    function(x, y, w, h) {
      draw_background(x, y, w, h)
      draw_tri_sc(x, y, w, h)
    },
    function(x, y, w, h) {
      draw_background(x, y, w, h)
      draw_bar(x, y, w, h)
    }
  ),
  grid_width  = unit(cell_w_cm * legend_key_scale, "cm"),
  grid_height = unit(cell_h_cm * legend_key_scale, "cm"),
  direction = "horizontal",
  nrow = 1,
  title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontfamily = "sans", fontface = "bold"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9, fontfamily = "sans")
)
```

### - Selecting relevant clinical metadata for visualisation

Here we subsets 'Clinical_metadata' to keep relevant features.

```{r}
colnames(Clinical_metadata) <- c('IPSS-M',
                                 'WHO',
                                 'ICC',
                                 'CK')
```

```{r}
# Subset Clinical_metadata to keep only certain columns
Clinical_metadata_selected <- Clinical_metadata[,c(
                                 'WHO',
                                 'ICC',
                                 'CK',
                                 'IPSS-M')]

# Subset Mutation_metadata to keep only the rows that have the same row names as Clinical_metadata_selected
Mutation_metadata <- Mutation_metadata[rownames(Clinical_metadata_selected),]
```

### - Defining categories and levels order

Here we convert several columns in Clinical_metadata_selected to factors with specific levels. We then rename the columns of 'Clinical_metadata_selected'.

```{r}
# Clinical_metadata_selected$Disease <- factor(Clinical_metadata_selected$Disease,
#                                                      levels = c('AML MRC', 'MDS', 'MPN', 'CH'))

Clinical_metadata_selected$`IPSS-M` <- factor(Clinical_metadata_selected$`IPSS-M`, 
                                                        levels = c('Very High',
                                                                   'High',
                                                                   'Moderate Low',
                                                                   'Low',
                                                                   'Very Low',
                                                                   'N/A'))

Clinical_metadata_selected$`CK` <- factor(Clinical_metadata_selected$`CK`, 
                                                     levels = c('Yes', 'No'))

Clinical_metadata_selected$`WHO class` <- factor(Clinical_metadata_selected$`WHO`, 
                                                     levels = c('Bi Allelic', 'Mono Allelic'))

Clinical_metadata_selected$`ICC class` <- factor(Clinical_metadata_selected$`ICC`, 
                                                     levels = c('Multi Hit', 'Single Hit'))

# Drop the raw WHO/ICC columns now that WHO class / ICC class exist,
# and set the display order: WHO class, ICC class, CK, IPSS-M
Clinical_metadata_selected <- Clinical_metadata_selected[, c('WHO class', 'ICC class', 'CK', 'IPSS-M')]
```

```{r}
Singlecell_metadata <- data.frame(row.names = rownames(Singlecell_data))

Singlecell_metadata$`SC class` <- factor(
  Singlecell_data$scDNAseq.Classification,
  levels = c('Bi Allelic', 'Mono Allelic')
)

# TP53 clone evolution (source column: TP53.clone.evolution). Rendered as
# coloured squares; 'Undetermined' shares the grey used for missing values.
# The Branching -> Parallel recode is retained defensively: the current CSV
# already uses 'Parallel', but older exports of this table did not.
clonal_raw <- as.character(Singlecell_data$TP53.clone.evolution)
clonal_raw[clonal_raw == 'Branching'] <- 'Parallel'
Singlecell_metadata$`TP53 clone evolution` <- factor(
  clonal_raw,
  levels = c('Linear', 'Parallel', 'Undetermined')
)

# Co-mutations (source column: Comutations). 'Co-occuring' and 'Independent'
# replace the previous Yes/No encoding; 'Both' covers patients carrying
# co-mutations of each kind, and 'N/A' shares the grey used for missing values.
Singlecell_metadata$`Co-mutations` <- factor(
  Singlecell_data$Comutations,
  levels = c('Co-occuring', 'Independent', 'Both', 'N/A')
)
```

### - Defining patients order

```{r}
# Carry the patient ID as an explicit column (dplyr verbs do not reliably keep
# row names) and extract its numeric index (e.g. 'PT04' -> 4) for ordering.
metadata_merged <- Clinical_metadata_selected
metadata_merged$Patient.ID <- rownames(Clinical_metadata_selected)
metadata_merged$pt_number  <- as.numeric(gsub("\\D", "", metadata_merged$Patient.ID))

# Split group = WHO class, with PT04 forced to Mono Allelic and everything else
# (including WHO class NA) assigned to Bi Allelic.
grp <- ifelse(as.character(metadata_merged$`WHO class`) == 'Mono Allelic',
              'Mono Allelic', 'Bi Allelic')
grp[is.na(grp)] <- 'Bi Allelic'
grp[metadata_merged$Patient.ID == 'PT04'] <- 'Mono Allelic'
metadata_merged$Group <- factor(grp, levels = c('Mono Allelic', 'Bi Allelic'))

# Order: Mono Allelic block first, then Bi Allelic; ascending patient number
# (01, 02, ...) within each block.
metadata_merged <- metadata_merged %>% arrange(Group, pt_number)

order <- metadata_merged$Patient.ID

Clinical_metadata_selected <- Clinical_metadata_selected[order,]
Laboratory_data <- Laboratory_data[order,1,drop=F]
Mutation_metadata <- Mutation_metadata[order,]

PTs_split <- data.frame(row.names = order)
PTs_split[,'Group'] <- metadata_merged$Group
PTs_split$Group <- factor(PTs_split$Group, levels = c('Mono Allelic', 'Bi Allelic'))
```

```{r}
Singlecell_metadata <- Singlecell_metadata[rownames(PTs_split),]
```

### - Heatmap columns metadata annotation colour

Here we define a list of color mappings for different categories in several variables.
The two single-cell tracks ('TP53 clone evolution' and 'Co-mutations') use
qualitative colours chosen to sit apart from the gold/red allelic scheme, the CK
browns and the IPSS-M greens. The 'Undetermined' and 'N/A' states reuse the
neutral grey used for missing values elsewhere, and 'Both' is an intermediate
tint between the two informative Co-mutations states, reflecting that it is a
mixture of them.

```{r}
# Define a list of color mappings for different categories in several variables
colors_top_annotation <-  list(
  # `Disease` = c('AML MRC' = '#822669',
  #               'MPN' = '#523183',
  #               'MDS' = '#24547f', 
  #               'CH' = '#40b6c9'
  #               ),
  `IPSS-M` = c('Very Low' = '#e7f8e9',
               'Low' = '#c9efcf',
               'Moderate Low' = '#95d5b2',
               # 'Moderate High' = '#52b788',
               'High' = '#2d6a4f',
               'Very High' = '#415942',
               'N/A' = '#D9D9D9'),
  `CK` = c('Yes' = '#7f4f24', 
                          'No' = '#b6ad90'),
  `WHO class` = c('Mono Allelic' = '#f9bc5a', 
                          'Bi Allelic' = '#b92831'),
  `ICC class` = c('Single Hit' = '#f9bc5a', 
                          'Multi Hit' = '#b92831'),
  `SC class` = c(
    'Mono Allelic' = '#f9bc5a',
    'Bi Allelic' = '#b92831'
  ),
  `TP53 clone evolution` = c(
    'Linear' = '#4E79A7',
    'Parallel' = '#8E6BAA',
    'Undetermined' = '#D9D9D9'
  ),
  `Co-mutations` = c(
    'Co-occuring' = '#2A9D8F',
    'Independent' = '#CDE7E3',
    'Both' = '#78BFB4',
    'N/A' = '#D9D9D9'
  )
)
```

### - Columns annotation

Here we create the heatmap annotations. Annotation track height is pinned to
`square_size`, which equals the column width, so each categorical block renders
as a square.

Top annotation: WHO class, ICC class, SC class. Bottom annotation: TP53 clone
evolution, Co-mutations, CK, IPSS-M. Every track is a simple categorical colour
map (coloured squares) with an automatically generated legend, so no
manually-built shape legends are required.

```{r}
n_genes <- ncol(Mutation_metadata)
n_patients <- nrow(Mutation_metadata)

# Top annotation order: WHO class, ICC class, SC class
top_annotation_df <- cbind(
  Clinical_metadata_selected[rownames(PTs_split), c('WHO class', 'ICC class')],
  `SC class` = Singlecell_metadata[rownames(PTs_split), 'SC class']
)

top_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  df = top_annotation_df,
  simple_anno_size = square_size,   # per-track height -> square cells
  gap = unit(0.75, "mm"),
  gp = gpar(lwd = 2, col = 'white'),
  col = colors_top_annotation, 
  show_annotation_name = T, 
  annotation_name_side = "left",
  show_legend = TRUE,
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontfamily = 'sans', fontface = 'bold'), 
  annotation_legend_param = list(
    `WHO class` = list(direction = "horizontal", nrow = 1),
    `ICC class` = list(direction = "horizontal", nrow = 1),
    `SC class`  = list(direction = "horizontal", nrow = 1)
  )
)

# Bottom annotation order: TP53 clone evolution, Co-mutations, CK, IPSS-M —
# all rendered as coloured squares.
bottom_annotation_df <- cbind(
  Singlecell_metadata[rownames(PTs_split), c('TP53 clone evolution', 'Co-mutations')],
  Clinical_metadata_selected[rownames(PTs_split), c('CK', 'IPSS-M')]
)

bottom_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  df = bottom_annotation_df,
  simple_anno_size = square_size,
  gap = unit(0.75, "mm"),
  gp = gpar(lwd = 2, col = "white"),
  col = colors_top_annotation,
  show_annotation_name = TRUE,
  annotation_name_side = "left",
  show_legend = TRUE,
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(
    fontsize = 10,
    fontfamily = "sans",
    fontface = "bold"
  ),
  annotation_legend_param = list(
    `TP53 clone evolution` = list(direction = "horizontal", nrow = 1),
    `Co-mutations`         = list(direction = "horizontal", nrow = 1),
    `CK`     = list(direction = "horizontal", nrow = 1),
    `IPSS-M` = list(direction = "horizontal", nrow = 1)
  )
)
```

### - Heatmap styling

Here we set custom padding for the column and row annotations in a heatmap.

```{r}
# Gap between the column annotations (top AND bottom) and the heatmap body
ht_opt$COLUMN_ANNO_PADDING = unit(20, "mm")   # bump for more space between anno and body

ht_opt$ROW_ANNO_PADDING = unit(0, "cm")
```

### - Heatmap plotting

Here we create an oncoprint. The body is sized directly from `cell_w_cm` and
`cell_h_cm`, so the drawn glyphs occupy exactly the space the geometry block
allocates them and the surrounding blank space is the requested row and column
gap. All annotation legends are placed horizontally along the bottom; the
detection legend is the hand-built `lgd_detection` object so its keys use the
same glyph code as the matrix.

```{r}
# Create an oncoprint
onco_print <- oncoPrint(
  t(Mutation_metadata[rownames(PTs_split), ]),
  alter_fun = alter_fun,
  alter_fun_is_vectorized = FALSE,
  get_type = get_type_fun,
  col = col,
  column_order = rownames(PTs_split),
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  remove_empty_rows = FALSE,
  pct_side = "right",
  border = FALSE,
  column_split = PTs_split,
  right_annotation = NULL,
  row_names_side = "left",
  show_pct = FALSE,
  pct_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontfamily = "sans"),
  row_names_gp = gpar(
    fontsize = 12,
    fontfamily = "sans",
    fontface = "italic"
  ),
  column_gap = unit(5, "mm"),
  left_annotation = NULL,
  show_heatmap_legend = FALSE,
  bottom_annotation = bottom_ha,
  top_annotation = top_ha,
  column_title = column_title,
  height = unit(cell_h_cm * n_genes,    "cm"),
  width  = unit(cell_w_cm * n_patients, "cm")
)

# Canvas size = fixed heatmap body PLUS a generous margin for everything drawn
# around it. The base numbers below ARE that margin:
#   - width base  -> room for the left-hand labels (annotation names such as
#     "TP53 clone evolution", plus the italic gene names) and the right-hand %
#     column, so nothing is clipped horizontally.
#   - height base -> room for the title, rotated column (patient) labels, and the
#     stacked horizontal legends along the bottom.
# The width base can likely be reduced now that the longest annotation name is
# "TP53 clone evolution" rather than "co-mutations in independent clone"; try
# 18 and check nothing clips before committing to it.
plot_width_cm  <- 24 + n_patients * cell_w_cm
plot_height_cm <- 34 + n_genes    * cell_h_cm

# Save PNG
png(
  filename = file.path(results_folder, "figures", "Fig_1A.png"),
  units = "cm",
  width = plot_width_cm,
  height = plot_height_cm,
  res = 300,
  type = "cairo"
)

draw(
  onco_print,
  annotation_legend_side = "bottom",
  annotation_legend_list = list(lgd_detection),
  merge_legends = TRUE,
  # outer margin (bottom, left, top, right): extra bottom for the legend rows
  # and extra left for the long annotation names so they clear the device edge.
  padding = unit(c(8, 10, 6, 8), "mm"),
  ht_gap = unit(6, "mm")
)

invisible(dev.off())

# Save PDF
pdf(
  file = file.path(results_folder, "figures", "Fig_1A.pdf"),
  width = plot_width_cm / 2.54,
  height = plot_height_cm / 2.54
)

draw(
  onco_print,
  annotation_legend_side = "bottom",
  annotation_legend_list = list(lgd_detection),
  merge_legends = TRUE,
  padding = unit(c(8, 10, 6, 8), "mm"),
  ht_gap = unit(6, "mm")
)

invisible(dev.off())
```

# 3) PTs subsets

```{r}
dir.create(path = paste(results_folder, '/figures/Additional', sep = ''), showWarnings = F)

for (selected_pt in rownames(Clinical_metadata_selected)) {
  
  Clinical_metadata_subset <- Clinical_metadata_selected[selected_pt, c('WHO class', 'ICC class', 'CK', 'IPSS-M')]
  Laboratory_data_subset <- Laboratory_data[selected_pt,1,drop=FALSE]
  Mutation_metadata_subset <- Mutation_metadata[selected_pt,]
  
  ###
  
  # Create a heatmap annotation object
  top_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    df = Clinical_metadata_subset[,], 
    gap = unit(0, "mm"),
    gp = gpar(lwd = 2.5, col = 'white'),
    col = colors_top_annotation, 
    show_annotation_name = T, 
    annotation_name_side = "left",
    show_legend = TRUE,
    annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontfamily = 'sans', fontface = 'bold'), 
    annotation_legend_param = list(
      `WHO class` = list(direction = "vertical"),
      `ICC class` = list(direction = "vertical"),
      `IPSS-M` = list(direction = "vertical"),
      `CK` = list(direction = "vertical")
    )
  )
  
  # Create a heatmap annotation object
  bottom_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    `Blast %` = anno_barplot(Laboratory_data_subset[rownames(Mutation_metadata_subset),'Blast.count']),
    gp = gpar(lwd = 2, col = 'white'),
    col = colors_top_annotation, 
    show_annotation_name = T, 
    annotation_name_side = "left",
    show_legend = TRUE,
    annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontfamily = 'sans', fontface = 'bold')
  )
  
  ###
  
  # Create an oncoprint
  oncoPrint <- oncoPrint(t(Mutation_metadata_subset),
                         alter_fun = alter_fun, 
                         alter_fun_is_vectorized = FALSE, 
                         get_type = get_type_fun,
                         col = col, 
                         show_column_names = TRUE,
                         remove_empty_rows = FALSE,
                         pct_side = "right", 
                         border = FALSE, 
                         right_annotation = NULL,
                         row_names_side = "left", show_pct = FALSE,
                         pct_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontfamily = 'sans'),
                         row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontfamily = 'sans', 
                                             fontface = 'italic'),
                         column_gap = unit(5, "mm"),
                         left_annotation = NULL, 
                         show_heatmap_legend = FALSE,
                         bottom_annotation = bottom_ha,
                         top_annotation = top_ha,
                         column_title = column_title)
  
  # Save the plot
  # Open a new PNG device for plotting
  png(filename = file.path(results_folder, 'figures/Additional',
                           paste0("Oncoprint", "_", selected_pt, ".png")), 
      units = "cm", width = 4.65*1.325, height = 13, res = 300, type='cairo')
  
  # Draw the oncoprint on the current plotting device
  draw(oncoPrint, 
       heatmap_legend_side = "right", 
       annotation_legend_side = "right",
       annotation_legend_list = list(lgd_detection),
       ht_gap = unit(6, "mm"))
  
  dev.off()
  
  
  pdf(file = file.path(results_folder, 'figures/Additional',
                       paste0("Oncoprint", "_", selected_pt, ".pdf")),
    width =  4.65*1.325 / 2.54, height = 13 / 2.54)
draw(oncoPrint,
     heatmap_legend_side = "right",
     annotation_legend_side = "right",
     annotation_legend_list = list(lgd_detection),
     ht_gap = unit(6, "mm"))
invisible(dev.off())
  
}
```
